description: The plot titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-3” illustrates how the sparsity ratio of SDPA output varies across model layers for three conditions (before gating, after gating, and after an average gate). The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer layers from 0 to 23 with major ticks shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 up to about 0.85 with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003,” which starts near about 0.01 at layer 0 and quickly drops to values very close to 0 by around layers 2–3, remaining near 0 through layer 23; an orange dotted line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126,” which begins near about 0.85 at layer 0, decreases steeply over early layers (around 0.4 by roughly layer 2 and around 0.15 by roughly layer 5), continues declining to near ~0.02 by around layers 12–16, then shows small fluctuations including a visible bump around layers ~19–22 (rising to roughly 0.05–0.08 near ~21) before ending around ~0.04–0.05 at layer 23; and a green dash-dot line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080,” which starts near about 0.80 at layer 0, drops sharply to roughly 0.28 by layer 1, then declines more gradually (around ~0.10 by about layer 4–5), approaching near-zero values by the mid-to-late layers (around ~0.01–0.02 near layers ~12–16) and ending close to 0 by layer 23.
